taxonomyNote: Formerly Hyla crucifer; some authors place western Pseudacris species in Hyliola but NatureServe notes this has not gained traction, and P. crucifer is unaffected.
fieldMarks: Small frog, about 20-25 mm (to 3.7 cm); gray, pink, brown, olive or yellowish above.
Dark X-shaped cross on the back (may be broken), a dark stripe from snout to eardrum and a dark bar between the eyes; dark bands on legs.
Toe tips enlarged into disks, hind toes only moderately webbed; belly cream or white.
Call is a single high piping whistle rising slightly, repeated about once a second; a chorus sounds like sleigh bells.
behavior: Mostly active at dusk and night but also by day in wet weather; males call from vegetation beside water or low in woody plants.
Eats small terrestrial invertebrates such as ants, beetles, flies and spiders; larvae eat algae and debris.
Calls from uplands in autumn, far from water; hibernates under logs and in tree holes; breeds early spring in the north.
habitat: Moist wooded areas near ponds, marshes, ditches and swamps, preferring fishless, often temporary pools with standing plants and debris.
range: Eastern North America from southeastern Manitoba east to the Atlantic, south to eastern Texas and mainland Florida (not the Florida Peninsula, per Animal Diversity Web). Introduced in Cuba.
